source.quote: The server MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path (hereafter referred to as the MCP endpoint) that supports POST.

requirements.exclusion: Endpoint topology — how many paths a server exposes and which methods each accepts — is deployment configuration; a recorded session shows one endpoint being used, never the set that exists. Same reasoning as TRAN-006 at 2025-11-25.

source.quote: Servers MUST validate the `Origin` header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks.

requirements.exclusion: Origin validation is server-internal policy applied before any MCP message; the trace records admitted sessions, not the requests a policy refused. Same reasoning as TRAN-002 at 2025-11-25; the everything server's policy middleware is tested directly in http_policy.rs.

source.quote: If the `Origin` header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.

requirements.exclusion: A refused request never becomes an MCP session, so the 403 it drew is outside what the tap records. Same reasoning as TRAN-007 at 2025-11-25; enforced in code and covered by the server's own policy tests.

source.quote: When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1) rather than all network interfaces (0.0.0.0).

requirements.exclusion: Bind address is process configuration with no wire footprint. Same reasoning as TRAN-008 at 2025-11-25.

source.quote: Servers SHOULD implement proper authentication for all connections.

requirements.exclusion: Authentication sits in front of the protocol; the authorization specification is out of scope for this registry for the reason `sources.json` records. Same reasoning as TRAN-009 at 2025-11-25.
